title: own experiment: AMD DPP/permlane warp_reduce_sum instead of shfl_xor loop
tg_gain_pct: tg128 +0.59% / +0.53% / +1.20% / +1.25% (dense, dense, MoE, Q4_0) on the idle machine -- none clears disjoint AND >=1%
notes: Own idea from the cross-backend sweep: Vulkan uses hardware subgroupAdd and CUDA >=Ampere uses __reduce_add_sync, but AMD falls through to a shfl_xor loop (5 rounds; gfx1201 reports warpSize=32, so wave32 not wave64 -- an earlier note saying 6 rounds on wave64 was wrong). Implemented with ds_swizzle + permlanex16 + permlane64, gated to gfx1100/1101/1102/1200/1201. Patch: patches/dpp_warp_reduce.diff. Run1 tg128 +1.09/+0.92/+1.29%; Run2 +1.01/+1.07/+4.93%. The +4.93% is inflated by a noisy OLMoE baseline ([219.60..245.86]); the patched side is stable across both runs ([247.29..249.31] and [247.91..249.26]), so the true MoE figure is ~+1.3% vs the clean baseline [245.24..245.71]. NOTE: an initial run was recorded as REJECTED (-6.82% MoE) -- that was GPU contention from Chrome/Parsec, not the kernel; the tell was a 15% spread on the patched side against 0.3% on the baseline. Small but uniform and free. RECLASSIFIED 2026-09-08 VALIDATED -> NEGLIGIBLE. Re-measured on the idle machine (chrome=0), 5 reps, vs frozen base: Qwen3-4B-Q4_K_M +0.59%, Qwen3-8B-Q4_K_M +0.53% (both disjoint ranges but under the 1% effect-size floor), OLMoE +1.20% and Q4_0 +1.25% (both overlapping ranges). Every cell is positive and correctness still passes (0 failing ops), but nothing satisfies our rule of disjoint ranges AND >=1% effect -- the same rule that demoted #27962 and #28178. The earlier +1.0/+1.3% VALIDATED verdict came from sessions with Parsec/Chrome/WebView active, which inflated the apparent effect by depressing the baseline. Not a v2 candidate on current evidence: ~0.5-1.2% for 42 lines of AMD-specific DPP intrinsics gated to five gfx targets. Kept in the database as a measured near-miss, not deleted. PROMOTED TO v2-candidate 2026-09-08 by explicit user decision, despite the NEGLIGIBLE status. Rationale on record: uniformly positive (+0.5-1.2% decode across 4 models), never negative on any cell, 0 failing ops. Status stays NEGLIGIBLE because it does not clear our disjoint-AND->=1% rule; the release field records the shipping decision, not the measurement verdict. MUST BE RE-MEASURED ON TOP OF #23685 before it is merged into a v2 stack: #23685 restructures lanes_per_block and the per-lane quant indexing that feed warp_reduce_sum, which is exactly what this patch replaces, so a sub-1% margin measured against the frozen base may not survive on top of it. They apply together cleanly (verified), but co-applying is not co-benefiting. REJECTED AND REMOVED FROM v2 2026-09-08. With the corrected correctness check (exit code + backend verdict, not just per-op ': FAIL' lines) DPP fails deterministically: 3 of 3 runs on the same binary give exit 1 with GATED_DELTA_NET, MUL_MAT_VEC_FUSION and TOPK_MOE failing, and the passing-op count collapses from ~14697 to ~12480, i.e. roughly 2200 cases lost. This is exactly the failure that broke the assembled v2 stack. The earlier '0 failing ops, twice' verdicts were produced by the broken parser and were wrong. Combined with its measured gain of only +0.5..1.2% -- at or below the ~0.95% noise floor -- there is no case for shipping it. The underlying observation still stands (AMD has no hardware reduction path where NVIDIA does); this particular implementation is not correct on our backend.

title: finding: the golden quality gate does not exercise decode-path (ncols_dst==1) kernels
tg_gain_pct: n/a - process defect, not an optimisation
gate: v1 re-gated on both legs: 0 failing ops; decode PPL -0.0144%; decode KLD 0.000859; batched KLD 0.002916
notes: Found while gating #23685. llama-perplexity evaluates in batches, so ncols_dst>1 and any optimisation gated on ncols_dst==1 is never executed. Instrumented count on the exact gate invocation: 252 selector calls, only 3 took the decode path -- the gate returned PPL identical to 4 dp, KLD exactly 0 and same-top-token 100%, i.e. it passed by testing code that did not run. Bit-exact KLD on a patch that changes activation quantization layout was the tell. FIX: add a decode leg to the gate (llama-perplexity -b 512 -ub 1) which forces ncols_dst==1; verified 7327/7327 calls take the packed path under -ub 1. APPLIES RETROACTIVELY: every decode-path change already shipped in v1 (#26301 dequant-to-float at ne11==1, #24386 MMVQ nwarps, DPP reduction) was gated only by the batched leg. They all passed test-backend-ops independently so this is not evidence they are wrong, but the gate had less power than claimed and the v1 stack should be re-gated with the decode leg. RESOLVED 2026-09-08: added the decode leg (llama-perplexity -b 512 -ub 1) and re-gated the v1 stack. THE DEFECT IS CONFIRMED BY DIRECT COUNT, not inference: an ne11 counter compiled into ggml_cuda_mul_mat shows the ORIGINAL batched gate ran mul_mat 8282 times with ne11==1 exactly ONCE (1/8282), while the new decode leg runs 7227/7227. So the gate that certified v1 never exercised the decode path where #26301 and #24386 live. RE-GATE RESULT: v1 PASSES both legs -- 0 failing ops, decode PPL 12.4893 -> 12.4875 (-0.0144%), decode KLD 0.000859 same-top 98.676%, batched KLD 0.002916 same-top 97.659% (batched leg reproduced the original run exactly, across a reboot). The decode path is in fact MORE faithful than the batched one, consistent with #25940/#28102 restructuring more arithmetic on the batched side. CONCLUSION: v1 quality claim was correct but previously untested; it is now actually verified. Gate script: goldengate2.ps1. Any future decode-path candidate must be gated with the -ub 1 leg.

title: own experiment: tune the RDNA4 ne11 threshold in ggml_cuda_should_use_mmvf (float matvec)
tg_gain_pct: none - current ne11<=8 is OPTIMAL for RDNA4; every lower threshold regresses 10-23% on both MoE models
gate: n/a - swept and rejected; control flat within +/-1.6%
notes: From the second cross-backend sweep. Gap is real: fp32_mma_hardware_available() admits CDNA only, so in ggml_cuda_should_use_mmvf the AMD F32 branch gives CDNA a measured 'ne11 <= 3' while RDNA4 falls to a blanket 'ne11 <= 8' that nobody tuned. INSTRUMENTED the mmvf dispatch branch in ggml_cuda_mul_mat and counted real calls: Qwen3-4B with -fa 1 = 0 hits; OLMoE with -fa 1 = 34 hits (all f32, ne01=64, the MoE router matmul); Qwen3-4B with -fa 0 = 144 hits (f16, ne01=256/128, the attention matmuls FA would otherwise absorb); OLMoE with -fa 0 = 98 hits. SO THE PATH IS LIVE -- an earlier claim that our quantized models never take it was wrong. It is nevertheless dead as a tuning target because max_ne11 == 1 in ALL FOUR runs: 1 satisfies both '<=3' and '<=8', so no value of the threshold alters dispatch on this workload. Would only matter for batched decode (ne11 2..8), the same blind spot as the MMVQ crossover candidate. INCIDENTAL: disabling flash attention costs Qwen3-4B -7.8% tg128 (126.82->116.89) and -22.9% pp512 (6007->4633), confirming our default benchmarks run with FA active. RE-OPENED AND TESTED 2026-09-08 once llama-batched-bench existed. Corrected scope first: F16 is ALREADY tuned for RDNA4 (should_use_mmvf line 844: RDNA4 -> ne11<=5), so the only untuned AMD path is F32, whose sole occurrence on our workload is the MoE router matmul f32[2048,64]. SWEPT T in {1,2,3,4} vs base(8) with batched-bench at npl 1,2,4,8 on OLMoE + gemma4-26B-A4B, with Qwen3-4B as a NULL CONTROL (probe showed zero mmvf calls there). RESULT: the current value is optimal and every reduction is a significant REGRESSION -- OLMoE B2 -19.9% at T=1, B4 -14.7..-16.1% at T=1..3, B8 -10.7..-11.8% at all T<8; gemma B4 -17.5..-17.7%, B8 -10.5..-11.2%. Control flat within +/-1.6% on every cell, and the damage always appears at exactly the ne11 value a given threshold newly excludes (T=4 leaves B4 at +0.4% but still breaks B8), so the pattern is coherent rather than noise. EXPLANATION: the gate is fp32_mma_hardware_available, which admits CDNA only. Architectures WITH fp32 matrix cores leave mmvf earlier because their alternative is better; RDNA4 has no fp32 MMA, so remaining on the float matvec kernel up to ne11=8 is correct. The permissive fallthrough is a correct consequence of the hardware, not an oversight. IMPORTANT METHODOLOGICAL NOTE: this falsifies the general inference "CDNA tuned + RDNA permissive => missed optimisation" that motivated this lead. RDNA4-MMVQ-XOVER rests on its own measurement, not on that pattern.

title: finding: build reproducibility broken, but no systematic perf offset; noise floor measured
tg_gain_pct: n/a - hypothesis NOT confirmed; build offset -0.56%..+0.32%, within a ~0.95% noise floor
notes: Observed while validating #28432 and #27044. Our A/B compares the STORED bin-baseline binaries against a FRESHLY COMPILED patched binary. In that batch every cell of both patches came out slightly negative (-0.17% to -1.51%), INCLUDING the dense control under #27044 -- a patch that only changes a buffer-size calculation on the MoE ids-path and cannot affect a dense model. That points to a systematic ~1% offset between cached and fresh builds rather than any patch effect. CONSEQUENCE: small positive effects are under-credited and small negatives exaggerated, in every A/B this project has run. Our disjoint-AND->=1% rule absorbs some of it but this is an unmeasured floor. FIX: run a NULL-PATCH CONTROL -- build the unmodified frozen base fresh and A/B it against bin-baseline; whatever difference appears is pure methodology and should be subtracted from, or at least reported alongside, sub-2% verdicts. NOT YET RUN. RESOLVED 2026-09-08 by a NULL-PATCH CONTROL: reverted to the frozen base with NO patch, rebuilt the identical source, and ran cached-vs-fresh-vs-cached (A/B/A) at 5 reps on 3 models. RESULT 1 -- MY HYPOTHESIS WAS WRONG: the build offset (fresh vs the mean of both cached runs) spans -0.56% to +0.32% with mean ~0, i.e. NO directional bias, and it is SMALLER than the pure run-to-run noise measured between the two cached runs of the identical binary (-0.95% to +0.46%). The uniformly negative cells in the #28432/#27044 batch were ordinary session variance that happened to land one way; I over-read a pattern from six cells. All previously recorded verdicts stand. RESULT 2 -- A DIFFERENT REAL DEFECT: the binaries are NOT byte-reproducible. ggml-hip.dll cached 74,917,888 b vs fresh 74,918,912 b, llama.dll 3,307,520 b vs 3,309,568 b -- different SIZES, so genuine code differences, not timestamps. The project's stated invariant 'revert must reproduce the byte-identical upstream DLL' is therefore FALSE and cannot be used as a build-correctness check. Most likely cause: bin-baseline predates today's project consolidation and CMake cache regeneration. Practical impact is nil (the perf delta is within noise) but the invariant should be dropped from the method description or bin-baseline rebuilt. RESULT 3 -- CALIBRATION: the same-binary noise floor reaches ~0.95% on pp512, so our >=1% effect-size rule sits directly on top of the floor and is only safe because disjoint ranges are ALSO required. Anything reported between 1% and 2% is near the floor -- notably DPP-reduce at +0.5..1.2%.

notes: Sweep item 4. ssm-scan.cu lines 345-765 are an SSD (State Space Duality) prefill path for Mamba-2, ~420 lines compiled out under '#if !defined(GGML_USE_HIP)', with the dispatch additionally requiring IS_NVIDIA && cc >= TURING. Gate is SSM_SSD_MIN_TOKENS=128 ('use_ssd = is_mamba2 && n_t > 128'), so on CUDA every prompt length we test would take it. MEASURED THE CURRENT HIP STATE FIRST rather than porting on faith. Prefill t/s by prompt length: mamba2-2.7b 2364/2518/2540/2540/2544 at p128/512/1024/2048/4096 -- essentially FLAT across a 32x range, exactly as linear-time theory predicts; Qwen3-4B for shape reference 4066/6041/5877/5590/5038, peaking then declining as quadratic attention bites. So Mamba-2 prefill on HIP is NOT pathological. It is however ~2x slower than a comparable transformer in absolute terms at every length, which is the headroom SSD exists to recover. DECISION DEFERRED, not abandoned: quantifying the prize needs an SSD-on vs SSD-off A/B, which is only possible on the NVIDIA side. BLOCKED: the box has CUDA toolkit v11.7 only, while the RTX 5060 Ti is Blackwell (compute 12.0) and needs CUDA 12.8+; the existing bin-cuda came from a prebuilt CUDA 13.3 release, which cannot be rebuilt with the SSD condition toggled. Options: install a newer CUDA toolkit (a user action), rely on upstream-reported SSD numbers (secondhand), or leave deferred. PRICED 2026-09-08 using the second GPU in the box. CUDA 13.3.1 toolkit installed (custom install, driver component excluded -- both display drivers verified unchanged afterwards), CUDA backend built from the SAME frozen base 73a43d1 for sm_120, build validated by Qwen3-4B tg128 126.69 against 126.63 from the earlier cross-backend study's prebuilt CUDA 13.3 binary (within 0.05%). EXPERIMENT: identical binary except one boolean -- 'const bool use_ssd = is_mamba2 && ...' short-circuited to false -- so the delta is SSD alone. RESULT on the 5060 Ti, prefill t/s at p128/512/1024/2048/4096: SSD on 3206/4856/4705/4815/4890, SSD off 3216/3606/3563/3611/3634, i.e. gains of -0.3%/+34.6%/+32.1%/+33.3%/+34.6%. TWO INTERNAL CONTROLS, both correct: (1) Qwen3-4B p512 measured 5860 with SSD on and 5857 with it off -- identical, as required since SSD is Mamba-only; (2) p128 shows -0.3%, because the gate is n_t > SSM_SSD_MIN_TOKENS with the constant at 128, so SSD genuinely does not fire at exactly 128 tokens. The mechanism confirms itself rather than merely failing to show noise. IMPLICATION: porting the ~420 HIP-excluded lines would plausibly buy ~33% on Mamba-2 prefill, moving our RDNA4 figure from 2518 t/s toward ~3350 at p512. COST: the path depends on CUB (NVIDIA-only; needs hipCUB or a rewrite) and on cuBLAS with 8-element alignment -- notable because our ROCm library-layer sweep found hipBLAS/rocBLAS entirely off the hot path for transformers, so this would deliberately bring it back in for Mamba-2. notes: Track B. Applies cleanly but FAILS TO BUILD, with every HIP translation unit erroring on 'common.cuh:1117: use of undeclared identifier GGML_TYPE_F8_E4M3'. title: Investigation: v1 test-backend-ops failures split into an upstream tolerance issue and one real regression
tg_gain_pct: n/a - correctness defect in the released stack
notes: RESOLVED by repeated-run measurement (12 runs per configuration, filtered to the affected op families so each run costs 35s instead of 150s). The intermittency is explained: test-backend-ops seeds init_tensor_uniform from std::random_device, so every run uses different input data and a case near its tolerance fails only on an unlucky draw. A single clean run therefore proves nothing. TWO SEPARATE CAUSES, and my first reading conflated them. (1) ADD / ADD_ADD on f16 is UPSTREAM, not ours: the frozen base fails it 3 runs in 12 on ADD(type=f16,ne=[10,5,4,3],nr=[2,1,1,1],nf=2) with errors 1.02e-7 to 1.07e-7 against a 1.0e-7 threshold -- 2 to 7 percent over, an f16 accumulation that upstream's tolerance does not quite allow for. Worth reporting upstream. My earlier claim that the base was clean came from a 3-run sample, too small to see a 25% rate. (2) FLASH_ATTN_EXT is OURS and is a genuine regression in #28102 -- see that row. ALSO CONFIRMED HERE: the original correctness parser counted only 'OP(...): FAIL' lines and never read the exit code or the 'Backend <name>: FAIL' summary, under which failures are listed as bare descriptors. Fixed permanently in scripts/opscheck.ps1, which reads all three signals and offers a repeated-run form. Exposure was limited: the 10 v2 candidates were each re-tested individually with the corrected check, and only DPP-reduce changed verdict. The remaining unverified 'ops 0 fail' rows are all NO_EFFECT or CORRECTNESS_ONLY entries that are not shipping.

title: Upstream: test-backend-ops ADD f16 tolerance is too tight, fails ~25% of runs on stock llama.cpp
tg_gain_pct: n/a - test-suite defect, no performance component
gate: frozen base: 4 of 20 FULL runs, 3 of 12 filtered
notes: Not our bug and not caused by any patch we carry. On the frozen base with no patches applied, ADD(type=f16,ne=[10,5,4,3],nr=[2,1,1,1],nf=2,perm1=0,src_overlap=0) and the related ADD_ADD(type=f16,type_addend=f16,ne=[64,5,4,3]) fail in roughly 1 run in 4, with errors 1.02e-7 to 1.07e-7 against a fixed 1.0e-7 threshold. The variation comes from init_tensor_uniform seeding a per-thread std::default_random_engine from std::random_device, so input data differs every run; the f16 accumulation sits just at the tolerance and an unlucky draw pushes it over. Practical consequences for this project: any single-run 'test-backend-ops passed' claim has about a 25% chance of a false failure, so verdicts must come from repeated runs, and a build showing only this ADD case should be read as clean. Worth reporting upstream once the ggml-org block lifts; the fix is a slightly looser tolerance for f16 ADD. CONFIRMED AND QUANTIFIED under full-suite conditions 2026-09-09: the unpatched base fails 4 of 20 full runs (ADD_ADD twice, ADD twice), the v2 stack 3 of 20 (ADD_ADD twice, ADD once). Margins on both sides run 1.00e-7 to 1.07e-7 against the 1.0e-7 threshold, including one run where the error EQUALLED the threshold and still counted as a failure. The rates are indistinguishable, so this family cannot be held against any patch stack.

title: v2 two-leg quality gate: passes on quality, blocked by one MUL_MAT_ID failure
tg_gain_pct: n/a - quality gate, not a performance measurement
gate: batched leg + decode leg, each perplexity run twice; 5 full test-backend-ops runs
notes: Stack under test: v1 minus 28102 (26301, 24386, 25940) plus the 9 candidates, DPP excluded. QUALITY: batched perplexity 9.1136 -> 9.1194 (+0.0636%, limit 0.5%); decode perplexity 12.4893 -> 12.4687 (-0.1649%); batched KLD 0.002894 with 97.929% same-top; decode KLD 0.00199 with 98.333% same-top, both against a 0.01 limit. Each perplexity leg was run twice and reproduced to 4 decimal places, base included. The decode leg is now genuinely covered: the ne11 probe recorded 7227 of 7227 mul_mat dispatches at ne11==1, against 1 of 8282 on the batched leg -- the blind spot that let the 28102 regression through the v1 gate. BLOCKER: 1 of 5 full test-backend-ops runs failed on MUL_MAT_ID(type_a=q4_K,type_b=f32,n_mats=4,n_used=1,b=0,m=512,n=1,k=256) -- MoE expert routing at decode width on q4_K. It did not appear in the 12 filtered runs (filtered to ADD/FLASH_ATTN_EXT) nor in the 3 earlier full runs, so the rate is low. Under investigation: 20 runs on the frozen base to establish whether it is upstream like the f16 ADD case, 20 on the v2 stack, then v2 minus each candidate in turn. The MMVQ-related candidates 23685 (hand-ported layout policy) and RDNA4-MMVQ-XOVER (q4_K/q6_K crossover) are tested first on suspicion, but the sweep covers all 9. RESOLVED -- see V2-GATE-2: it did not recur in 28 further full runs, and the unpatched base produces the same class of marginal failure. v2 is releasable. TWO HARNESS BUGS FOUND AND FIXED WHILE RUNNING THIS: (1) the gate script used $P for the patches directory and $p as a loop variable -- PowerShell variable names are case-insensitive, so the loop overwrote the path and every apply failed with "can't open patch '26301/stack_26301.diff'"; renamed to $pn. (2) every script in this project applied patches as 'git apply ... 2>&1 | Out-Null', silently ignoring failures, so a run could report success while building a stack with a patch missing. Applies are now checked, the tracked-file count is logged before and after each patch, and the files 26301 adds are asserted present.

title: MUL_MAT_ID resolved: marginal quantized-matvec tolerance, present on the unpatched base too
tg_gain_pct: n/a - correctness measurement
gate: 40 filtered runs + 40 full runs, v2 and frozen base side by side
notes: The blocker from V2-GATE-1 was a single MUL_MAT_ID(type_a=q4_K,type_b=f32,n_mats=4,n_used=1,b=0,m=512,n=1,k=256) failure in 1 of 5 full gate runs. MEASUREMENT: filtered -o MUL_MAT_ID gave 0 of 20 on the base and 0 of 20 on v2; that form cannot be trusted alone, because running 880 cases in isolation changes allocation pattern, preceding GPU state and the random draws, so the full suite was repeated 20 times per side under exactly the gate's conditions. RESULT: v2 failed 3 of 20 and the base 4 of 20, and MUL_MAT_ID did not recur once on either side -- so 1 occurrence in 28 full runs of v2 in total. DECISIVE EVIDENCE: base run 19 failed MUL_MAT(type_a=q5_1,type_b=f32,m=16,n=1,k=32) with err 0.000508888 against a 0.000500000 threshold, 1.8% over. That is the same class of event as the MUL_MAT_ID case -- the sibling op, the same n=1 decode width, a quantized type, and a margin a hair over tolerance -- occurring with NO patches applied. So the unpatched base itself produces marginal quantized-matvec failures at n=1 at roughly 1 in 20. HONEST LIMIT: the gate script logged the failing case string but not its ERR margin, so the magnitude of our one MUL_MAT_ID event was never captured and this remains strong supporting evidence rather than proof. The scripts now always log margins, so a recurrence would settle it immediately. Compare the FLASH_ATTN_EXT regression in 28102, which was 1.6x to 8x over tolerance, reproduced readily, and was absent from the base -- that is what a real fault looks like against this backdrop.

title: Gate pass rule updated: distinguish upstream marginal-tolerance failures from real faults
tg_gain_pct: n/a - harness policy
notes: Measured on this hardware, stock llama.cpp at 73a43d1 fails test-backend-ops in 4 of 20 full runs with no patches applied. A gate that treats any single failing run as a blocker therefore rejects the unpatched upstream code about 20% of the time, which is how the original one-run gate could pass v1 while it carried a real regression -- it was a coin toss either way. THE RULE NOW: (1) never judge correctness from a single run, because init_tensor_uniform seeds from std::random_device and every run uses different input data; (2) always record the ERR = actual > threshold margin, since that is what separates a case sitting on the tolerance line from a genuine fault; (3) compare against the frozen base measured over the SAME number of runs, not against an assumption that the base is clean; (4) a failure is upstream-class if it also occurs on the unpatched base at a comparable rate AND its margin is within a few percent of threshold -- currently the f16 ADD/ADD_ADD family and marginal quantized matvec at n=1. Anything reproducible, absent from the base, or far over tolerance is ours and blocks the release.
